In the last three months, Spetic has been as good as advertised and arguably has become Texas' No. 1 player out of the transfer portal. And that might not be a stretch. Wide receiver Cam Coleman peaked early, then hurt his shoulder and gave way to freshman Jermaine Bishop Jr. Up front, Melvin Siani, Dylan Sikorski and Laurence Seymore III came to solidify the offensive line, but that's been a trouble spot all season. OK, Rasheem Biles has been pretty good. Special, even. In fact, the linebacker transfer from Pitt has truly been outstanding as one of best at his position in school history and a sure-fire first-team All-American and probably the real Longhorn MVP among every-down players. (Biles, too, hails from Ohio roots, so Sarkisian ought to consider grabbing about 20 portal additions from that state in January.) It's also true that Colin Simmons got most of the headlines in 2026 and could be considered the MVP. And the junior edge rusher, who has been one of college football's premier edge rushers with 10½ sacks in his first five games, has stamped himself as one of the best Longhorn defenders in the program's history and a finalist for the Nagurski Trophy. However, he sat out two games entirely with a high ankle sprain, played just 18 snaps against Missouri and didn't have a tackle and last Saturday heavily impacted the win over LSU with eight tackles. But Spetic has been nails. As a bit of a history lesson, Texas only knows successful kickers. From Happy Feller to Russell Erxleben, from Phil Dawson to Justin Tucker, from Kris Stockton and Hunter Lawrence to Cameron Dicker, the school could stake its claim as Kicker U. Never mind no Longhorn has ever won the Lou Groza Award, a huge oversight, because it's had four first-team All-Americans, including three-time honoree Erxleben. Anthony Fera was the last Horn so recognized in 2013. Spetic falls in line with those deadeye kickers. Spetic has shown such reliability that he's been borderline automatic. He leads all kicker with 10 field goals without a whiff against Top 25 teams. Just don't tell him that. He doesn't want to jinx himself. So how much range does he have? "Probably from 60, I'm confident," said Spetic, whose career long is from 52 yards. "Sixty and in would be good, I'd say." Texas kicker Gianni Spetic (44) celebrates after a field goal during the game against LSU at Tiger Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Most recently, he booted three field goals of 41 yards or longer, including a 50-yarder last Saturday to put Texas in position for the game-winning drive and clinching touchdown over LSU with three seconds to play to hang on for a 22-21 victory. He kicked two to keep Texas close in the Missouri game before Arch Manning's third touchdown pass and Graceson Littleton's takeaway sealed the win. Texas Longhorns kicker Gianni Spetic (44) kicks a field goal during the game against Missouri at Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium in Columbia on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. (Mikala Compton/Austin American-Statesman) Spetic was true on both attempts in the narrow 34-27 win over Ole Miss. He kicked a pair of them to beat Tennessee 20-17 at Neyland Stadium. Against UTSA at home, he drove three through the uprights. Some may have forgotten, but Spetic also made a 37-yarder in the second quarter to get Texas on the board against Ohio State before a heroic, 20-point comeback in the second half. He's been that good, that consistent. He's made his last nine in a row, "and they really haven't been chip shots," Sarkisian said. "He's off to a heckuva start." Stepic may be so good that he could save Jeff Banks' job as Sarkisian sidekick and special teams coordinator as well as Texas' season. Banks found him after being alerted to Spetic's background. Spetic's older brother, Emilio, was a Division III soccer player at Mount Union in 2022 on the same team with Sarkisian's nephew Ryan. Emilio recommended Gianni as a senior at Notre Dame Cathedral Latin to Ryan's father Dave, who is Steve Sarkisian's brother. Trouble was Texas was up to its ears in kickers on its 2023 roster. The USC Trojans are coming into their matchup against the Tarleton State Texans on Thursday evening looking to add to their four-game win streak to begin the 2026-27 college basketball season. However, the team is going to be short-handed. Both Onyeka Joe Agu and Eric Reibe were ruled out for USC due to injury, as per Jon Rothstein of 247Sports.com Onyeka Joe Agu is nursing a groin injury while Eric Reibe is dealing with a foot injury for USC‘s game against Tarleton State. Neither player has suited up for the Trojans yet this season. Agu is a freshman whole Reibe is a sophomore. Reibe transferred to USC via the portal after spending his freshman season at UConn. The young big man appeared in 40 games for the Huskies, including five starts, at a little over 13 minutes per game. He averaged 5.9 points and 3.3 rebounds with splits of 65.8 percent shooting from the field, 30.8 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 52.1 percent shooting from the free-throw line. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The 20-year-old suffered the injury during the offseason , a re-aggravation of a previous injury, and is in the rehab process following surgery. Reibe was expected to play a key role for the Trojans this season as he continues his development. With Joe Agu, the amount of playing time and role he would have had with USC this season was a little less certain. He was part of a heralded recruiting class for the Trojans that included five-star twin centers Darius and Adonis Ratliff, and five-star forward Christian Collins. Joe Agu joined the team after beginning his basketball career in his home country of Belgium. He most recently played in the BNXT league, a joint basketball venture between Belgium and the Netherlands. item.title: Pelicans point out 10 reasons why ‘special’ Herb Jones still worth first round pick
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images Pelicans point out 10 reasons why ‘special’ Herb Jones still worth first round pick appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . As the February 11 trade deadline slowly comes into view, critical chatter around the New Orleans Pelicans has only gotten louder. EVP Joe Dumars and GM Troy Weaver stuck with a relatively status quo roster to start the Jamahl Mosley era, with a 5-11 record to show for it. This reality has only served as fuel when it comes to rumors about Herb Jones and Trey Murphy III’s future in the Big Easy. Murphy III has the most trade market value by all accounts, with the Pelicans holding firm at three first-round picks in return. This would match the deal for Desmond Bane, another near-All-Star who was moved recently. Beyond that, league sources have long indicated New Orleans is also holding firm on an asking price of two first-round picks (one protected) for the versatile wing, even as his minutes fluctuated under Mosley. Jones has been linked to several contenders, including the Oklahoma City Thunder, Golden State Warriors, Portland Trail Blazers, Miami Heat, and Los Angeles Lakers. There are more suitors snooping around the Smoothie King Center as well, so the market is robust. Mosley, who has been playing Jones more often, gave the NBA a list of 10 reasons why EVP Joe Dumars is holding firm on what ClutchPoints first reported as a ‘ridiculous’ asking price . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Herb’s a winner. I don’t think there’s any other way to put it. He’s a winner. He’s a professional. He’s a team guy. He is about whatever it takes to get the job done. And that’s what he brings to this team. He brings our locker room together with the way he communicates, the way guys feed off of his energy,” Mosley told ClutchPoints. “And then defensively, he just does special things. Being able to play the passing lane, being physical, making sure he’s getting tags and hits on the rollers, but also chasing over screens. He does all of the little things that help you get to wins.” Sounds like the Pelicans will stick to their asking price. However, skeptics have real numbers on their side. Jones shot 38.3% from the field and 30.9% from beyond the arc last season, and he’s in the final year of his current deal before a larger extension begins next season. Locked in at roughly $14.9 million this season before scaling to $20.9 million in 2027–28 (with a $24.2 million player option for 2029–30), Jones gives buyers high-impact two-way value at a manageable cap number. Still, any team paying two firsts is betting that his defense and glue-guy value outweigh the shooting. item.title: Rick Bowness returns to the 'fight' with Columbus Blue Jackets
item.description: Rick Bowness isn't cleared to lace up his skates yet, but the veteran NHL coach is returning to the Blue Jackets' bench Nov. 19 in Chicago. More: Columbus Blue Jackets drop fifth straight game: 5 reasons they're losing After missing three games while dealing with an unspecified health condition , the 71-year-old coach said he is eager to help his team end a five-game losing streak when they play the Chicago Blackhawks in the second leg of a four-game road trip. "It’s weird watching the games," Bowness told reporters Nov. 19 in Chicago. "It’s a little different. You’d rather be here with the guys. You want to be in the fight. That’s the biggest thing. So, it’s good to be back and get back in the fight with these guys.” Bowness said he gained a new perspective watching games on television, and some of it came from his wife, Judy, who offered her own thoughts on the Blue Jackets' woes. "I learned from her," Bowness said. "She was pointing things out, but you see things differently, a little more objectively. You’re not in the moment. So, you get a totally different look." After watching the Blue Jackets melt down in the third period of a 5-1 loss to the New York Islanders to start the trip Nov. 17, he'd had his fill of watching from afar. It took some convincing, but he eventually met up with the Blue Jackets at their Nov. 18 practice in Chicago. "[The medical staff] didn’t like what I was telling them," Bowness said. "Let’s put it that way." Bowness explained his situation to the team at practice, saying that he's cleared to coach in games from the bench but not to join them for on-ice work yet. Asked if he's still fighting off whatever caused the absence, Bowness sounded like a hockey player who's dealing with an injury. “Oh yeah, we’re good," he said. "We're here. That’s all that matters. We’re here. Jump in with them again [on the bench].” Bowness hopes to gain clearance for skating in practices by Nov. 21, when the Blue Jackets will hold either a full or optional morning skate in Toronto. Until then, he'll settle for running the bench in Chicago with assistants Don Granato, Trent Vogelhuber and Jared Boll. "I missed a week," Bowness said. "That’s a long time, so I’m thrilled to be back.” Dispatch Blue Jackets/Crew reporter Brian Hedger can be reached at bhedger@dispatch.com This article originally appeared on The Columbus Dispatch: Rick Bowness returns to the 'fight' with Columbus Blue Jackets

item.title: Jesper Svensson, Michael Thorbjornsen share low score in the rain and win at Sea Island in PGA Tour finale
item.description: ST. SIMONS ISLAND, Ga. — Michael Thorbjornsen spent the last few weeks working on his iron play and saw it pay off Thursday in the rain and wind at Sea Island. He made five of his seven birdies inside 10 feet for a 6-under 64 to share the low score with Jesper Svensson in the RSM Classic. Thorbjornsen, one of the group of rising young stars who won the Rocket Classic this year for his first PGA Tour title, had five birdies in a seven-hole stretch around the turn at the tougher Seaside course, which included an 8-foot par save. Svensson, who needs at least a two-way tie for second to finish among the top 100 in the FedEx Cup to keep a full card for next year, birdied his last four holes on the easier Plantation course for an 8-under 64. Max Greyserman and Garrick Higgo each shot 65 on the Plantation, while Sea Island member Keith Mitchell shot 65 at Seaside. The final tournament of the PGA Tour brings different levels of pressure, mainly for those who want to be fully exempt next year by finishing in the top 100. Greyserman, who came in at No. 91 and should be safe, only thinks about posting the best score he can. Emiliano Grillo (No. 113) is well aware what’s at stake. “Everybody knows what they need to do out there,” Grillo said after a 66 at Plantation. “Yeah, good start. Hopefully many more of these. I know what I need to do and it was good.” Thorbjornsen is among nine players in the field who finished in the top 50 on the PGA Tour and are exempt for all the $20 million signature events. He felt the missing piece was his iron game, not giving himself enough birdie chances. “We’ve worked very hard on my irons, just having more control,” Thorbjornsen said. “My driving stats have been pretty decent these past couple years and I haven’t really been able to take advantage of it. So trying to get the ball closer to the hole. That gives you more birdie looks but also less bogey chances.” Ten of the top 16 players on the leaderboard to par came into the week outside the top 100. Svensson is at No. 135. He spent most of his day trying to keep himself and his golf clubs dry and negotiating a wind that wasn’t as strong as practice rounds but no less a nuisance. The Swede had seven birdies on the back nine at Plantation and only wants to keep going. “You can’t really deny the situation that you’re in,” Svensson said. “Not really thinking of it when you’re playing as much as trying to hit the right areas and hit some good shots. item.title: Shelton beats Jodar to reach last four of ATP Finals for first time
item.description: US tennis player Ben Shelton in action against Spain's Rafael Jodar during their men's singles match of the 2026 Nitto ATP Finals, an international tennis match in Turin. (is associated with: «Shelton beats Jodar to reach last four of ATP Finals for first time») Mickael Chavet/ZUMA Press Wire/dpa US Open runner-up Ben Shelton is into the last four of the ATP Finals for the first time after beating Rafael Jodar. Shelton had to dig deep to see off the 20-year-old Spaniard, who is completing his first season on the ATP Tour, but eventually prevailed 7-6 (10-8) 7-5. His place in the semi-finals was then confirmed as world number one Alexander Zverev fought his way to a 6-4 7-6 (8-6) win over Frenchman Arthur Fils in the final match of the day. Shelton only lost his serve once but still needed more than two hours to see off Jodar, who forced a couple of break points in the opening set. Speaking on court after the match, Shelton said he would be watching Zverev’s contest with Fils and rooting for the German, who was already assured of top spot in the John McEnroe group after going through the round robin unbeaten. And Shelton would have liked what he saw as Zverev advanced in straight sets, albeit needing a tiebreaker in a second set which did not see a single break of serve. But Fils already knew at that point he was heading out, having needed a straight-sets win to stay alive in the tournament. In the doubles, Britain’s Henry Patten and Finnish partner Harri Heliovaara – the Wimbledon champions – saw their title defence ended as they lost 7-6 (7-5) 7-6 (7-3) to French pair Theo Arribage and Albano Olivetti. item.title: Drone footage of Pochettino’s Man Utd training session posted online
item.description: FILE PHOTO - USA manager and new Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino during press conference at the Arthur M. Blank National Training Centre. (is associated with: «Drone footage of Pochettino’s Man Utd training session posted online») Press Association/PA Wire/dpa Footage from Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session as Manchester United manager has appeared online after being captured by a drone operator. A 12-minute video of the session was posted onto YouTube after being captured at United’s Carrington training ground. Pochettino and his United players can be seen in the video, with the squad having been divided into three groups. On the post, the drone operator wrote: “For the people asking about legality. It is unrestricted airspace, meaning anyone can fly over it. “The drone remained in line of sight at all times, it didn’t fly over anyone or even near anyone so was a perfectly legal flight going by the CAA rules that regulates drone usage. “The drone is correctly labelled, and I hold all the relevant licences, public liability and insurance required. As for leaking team news/tactics, it was half an hour into the manager’s first training session, there are many media there so certainly won’t be the only footage of training released.” Manchester United have declined to comment. Pochettino was taking his first training session after being appointed as United’s new head coach last week, succeeding Michael Carrick who was sacked with the club in the relegation zone during this international window. Pochettino arrived in Manchester on Wednesday, having taken charge of the United States for the final time in their 2-0 win over Haiti, which finished in the early hours of Wednesday morning UK time. His first match in charge will be a visit to old rivals Liverpool on Sunday afternoon.

item.title: Troy Aikman Adds Fire to Ongoing Joe Buck Feud with Dig About Wanting a ‘One-Man Booth’
item.description: Joe Buck, Troy Aikman Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect NEED TO KNOW Troy Aikman joked about his Monday Night Football partner in his weekly radio spot Thursday The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback seemingly advanced his feud with Joe Buck Buck has negotiated a new contract, while Aikman’s future on the flagship program is uncertain Troy Aikman didn’t fumble the chance to throw Joe Buck under the bus. While in his weekly guest spot on The Musers radio show on Dallas-Fort Worth’s The Ticket 96.7 on Thursday, Nov. 19, the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback had a laugh at his Monday Night Football partner’s expense. “You wanna come in, just hang out?” host George Dunham asked the Hall of Famer, after he shared that he was “flying solo” without his usual co-host Craig Miller. “Joe’s always wanted a one-man booth, I’m wondering if you’ve always wanted a one-man radio show?” Aikman, 59, said, laughing. Troy Aikman and Joe Buck in October 2024. Credit: USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect All of which had Dunham, 61, cracking up as well. “Joe and I have a lot in common,” Dunham replied. “Yeah, saw him on the Country [Music] Awards last night. He’s everywhere.” Aikman then replied, still chuckling: “Yeah, everywhere … ubiquitous.” Despite bringing the jokes, Aikman views his future on MNF as seemingly not a laughing matter. Over the past few weeks while calling their weekly games, viewers have called out the broadcasters’ increasingly frosty exchanges and body language. Earlier this week, ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro called the storyline surrounding their ongoing feud “ disappointing ,” particularly in advance of the network’s first-ever Super Bowl broadcast in February. item.title: Mauricio Pochettino could target a Barcelona star as his first Man United signing
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino could target a Barcelona star as his first Man United signing A member of the defensive ranks at La Liga champions Barcelona has this week been linked with a fresh move to the Premier League, with Manchester United. The Blaugrana star in question? Alejandro Balde. It has of course proven to be a busy last few days behind the scenes at Manchester United. After finally making the call to part ways with Michael Carrick, the Old Trafford brass appointed Mauricio Pochettino in the Englishman’s place. ‘Poch’, for his part, already has one eye on the January transfer window, where he is eyeing reinforcements to his Red Devils squad. One area in need of fresh blood in the eyes of the Argentine is left-back, where a shortlist of targets has already been drawn up, featuring the names of the likes of Lewis Hall and Antonee Robinson. Also on the radar of Pochettino and co. following summer transfer links between the parties, though, is the aforementioned Alejandro Balde. As per a report from Mundo Deportivo , citing the Manchester Evening News, owing to both his age and experience at a top club, Balde is considered a legitimate potential addition at Old Trafford. Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Drone footage posted on YouTube of Mauricio Pochettino’s first Man United training session
item.description: Drone footage showing Mauricio Pochettino leading his first training session as Manchester United manager has been posted online. The 12-minute clip, which was filmed above United’s Carrington training complex, was uploaded to YouTube . In the video, Pochettino can be seen working alongside the squad, which had been split into three separate groups. Addressing the upload, the drone operator wrote: "For the people asking about legality. It is unrestricted airspace, meaning anyone can fly over it. "The drone remained in line of sight at all times, it didn’t fly over anyone or even near anyone so was a perfectly legal flight going by the CAA rules that regulates drone usage. "The drone is correctly labelled, and I hold all the relevant licences, public liability and insurance required. As for leaking team news/tactics, it was half an hour into the manager’s first training session, there are many media there so certainly won’t be the only footage of training released." Man United are currently in the relegation zone (Getty) Manchester United have declined to comment on the footage. The session marked Pochettino’s opening training session following his appointment as United’s new head coach last week. He succeeds Michael Carrick, who was dismissed during the international break with the team currently in the relegation zone after winning just one of their 10 Premier League matches. After overseeing his final match with the United States - a 2-0 victory over Haiti that concluded early on Wednesday morning UK time - Pochettino arrived in Manchester later that day. His first match in charge will see United take on old rivals Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday afternoon. Andoni Iraola’s side are currently 10 points above United in the table, and will be hoping to spoil Pochettino’s Premier League return. Pochettino is taking charge of his fourth Premier League club, having previously managed Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. However, he has made it clear that he has been an admirer of United for a long time, and was cheering them on when they completed the Treble by winning the 1999 Champions League final against Bayern Munich in Barcelona. “I was in Barcelona in that final, that was an iconic final,” he said in his first interview as manager. “We were shouting for Manchester United. “From there, it was so exciting to see Manchester United, and more with the admiration of Sir Alex Ferguson – for me, the best coach in the history of the sport. I always admired him.”

item.title: Lakers legend Kurt Rambis a fan of CV Lakers G League move to desert
item.description: The Coachella Valley Lakers are back home at Acrisure Arena after a fine 4-1 start with a pair of games against the Stockton Kings on Thursday and Friday. And if you're already starting to feel like you know this team or if you're a diehard Los Angeles Lakers that likes to know what's happening down on the farm, there's a new podcast you should probably know about. It's called the Dribble & Dust podcast and it's hosted by Judd Spicer and it's a podcast entirely focused on the CV Lakers. The inaugural episode took place before the season started as Spicer had a loaded roundtable discussion with Lakers legend Kurt Rambis and entertainment icon and Oak View Group co-founder, Irving Azoff. It was a fascinating chat, including how Rambis and Azoff met during Ramis' playing days with the Lakers thanks to a burly assist from 76ers big man Darryl Dawkins. Rambis and Azoff talked about the Coachella Valley Lakers and what fans can expect at Acrisure Arena this year, and why the move was a positive one for the Lakers, the players and the valley. Rambis said that while he's excited to see how much this team means to the valley, we shouldn't forget that this move to Acrisure Arena means a lot to the players both personally and in their development. "For them to play in an arena is much better than playing in our practice facility that sat about 400 people," Rambis said. "To give them an environment where they are feeling like like they are in a real basketball game in front of a loud audience is going to be meaningful to them and help their development as well because playing in a big arena is where they hope to be headed." The Desert & Dust Podcast is brought to you each time by title sponsor Desert Willow Golf Resort and will also feature a segment sponsored by Gear to the Max in which Spicer talks to a member of the sports staff of The Desert Sun, which is the local newspaper in what is now CV Lakers country. Give the inaugural podcast a listen right here. item.description: Luke Littler became world number one for the first time when he won the Grand Slam of Darts in 2025 [Press Association] The 2026 Grand Slam of Darts is under way and another of the Professional Darts Corporation's (PDC) major titles is set to be won in Wolverhampton. This edition is bigger than ever, with 48 players taking part, and unlike most of darts' major tournaments, the players are split into groups in the initial phase, rather than a straight knockout format. Each player will face two opponents in their group, with only the group winner progressing into the last 16. The rest of the competition is a straight knockout format. Luke Littler is the defending champion following a 16-11 victory over Luke Humphries in the 2025 final to become world number one for the first time. However, his hopes of a third successive title were ended by Jermaine Wattimena in the second round. When is the Grand Slam of Darts? The tournament lasts for nine days from Saturday, 14 November to Sunday, 22 November. Group stage (14-17 November) - 48 matches Second round (18-19 November) - eight matches Quarter-finals (20-21 November) Semi-finals (22 November) Final (22 November) What is the format? In the group stage, the format is best of nine legs, or first to five legs. In the initial phase, two points are awarded for a win, with the group winner progressing to the last 16. In case of players being level on points at the end of the group phase, the following tie-breakers apply: Total Leg Difference Total Legs Won Total Legs Won Against Throw Highest Total Tournament Average (to two decimal places) Highest Winning Match Average (to two decimal places) A play-off - nine-dart leg Second-round matches are a best-of-19 format, or first to 10 legs. The quarter-finals, semi-finals and final are best of 31 legs, or first to 16 legs. Who is playing and how did they qualify? With the tournament expanded, a new set of qualification rules have been put in place. Up to 24 players could qualify from reaching a major PDC televised final in the past 12 months, but only nine ended up qualifying via that route, partly because of the dominance Littler has shown. Ten players reached Wolverhampton from the PDC youth, development and challenge tours, the Women's Matchplay and Women's Series and championships from across the globe. Six more secured places through the European Tour, while 13 qualified with a Players Championship win. The final 10 spots, which include ninth seed Stephen Bunting, were claimed in a PDC tour card holder qualifying event. item.title: UEFA Women's Champions League: Bayern Frauen await next month's Barça Femení test as the holders and OL Lyonnes advance to quarters
item.description: UEFA Women's Champions League: Bayern Frauen await next month's Barça Femení test as the holders and OL Lyonnes advance to quarters FC Bayern Frauen secured qualification to the knockout stages of the UEFA Women's Champions League with a comfortable 4-0 victory over bottom-placed Austria Wien . Jose Barcala’s side drew their home games against Manchester City and PSG, but they extended their perfect away record in Vienna. However, that wasn't enough for a guaranteed top-four finish before the league phase concluded next month. The eight teams finishing outside the automatic quarter-final spots will enter an extra playoff round. Bayern are currently third in the standings, but five teams stand a chance to leapfrog them on the final matchday. FC Bayern will host holders Barcelona in mid-December as they will hope to avenge their 7-1 defeat at a similar stage last year as well as the semi-final loss. For the Spanish giants, they will be under no pressure as they secured their place in the last four with a 6-0 victory over Servette on Thursday. Similarly, leaders OL Lyonnes are through after a brilliant 2-0 win at the 2024/25 winners Arsenal. Germany international Jule Brand opened the scoring for the visitors with her first goal in two months for the Première Ligue leaders. Chelsea and OL Lyonnes are yet to concede a goal in this season's competition, but the latter lost their starting spot to Barça on goal difference. The four-time champions have a five-goal-per-game ratio before ending their league phase campaign in Unterhaching.

item.title: Mikel Arteta dealt fresh injury blow as Arsenal prepare for Newcastle United
item.description: Mikel Arteta's Gunners could be without three players against Newcastle United -Credit:David Price, Arsenal FC via Getty Images Martín Zubimendi has handed Mikel Arteta a fresh injury concern ahead of Arsenal's trip to St James' Park to take on Newcastle United. The Gunners head to Tyneside on Saturday looking to maintain their momentum at the summit of the Premier League table, with club soccer finally returning after the international break. Arteta's side have strung together five consecutive top-flight victories to establish a five-point lead at the top — and they remain firmly on course to defend their title. -Credit:Sebastian Frej, Getty Images However, the manager faces a couple of injury concerns heading into the fixture. Bukayo Saka continues his recovery from the quad injury sustained in the UEFA Champions League match against Bayern Munich, and it remains doubtful he will be fit enough to feature against the Magpies. Speaking ahead of Arsenal's most recent victory over Hull City, Arteta was guarded about Saka's potential return date. He said via football.london : "We're talking obviously about weeks. Let's see after the international break. "He's going to start hitting the pitch and start to have more activity and see how he feels, but unfortunately he's going to be out for a while. "I don't want to put these guys under too much pressure. They are doing their best to get back fit, Bukayo is desperate to get back with the team, but it's still quite early." Noni Madueke has shone as his replacement, but Arteta will be eager to have his star winger available again as they brace for the congested holiday fixture calendar. To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE Zubimendi represents another fitness worry for Arteta, having sustained what looked like a hamstring problem in Spain's loss to England on Sunday. The midfielder featured in his second consecutive match for the world champions and seemed to experience some muscular discomfort, which will sound warning signals for Arsenal. Arteta will provide an update on the midfielder - who has found regular playing time hard to come by this season - during his pre-Newcastle press conference on Friday. One player certain to be absent for the Newcastle clash is Max Dowman, who will complete the last match of his three-game suspension for the red card he picked up in the surprising Carabao Cup loss to Fleetwood Town. item.title: Celtics rookie creates fascinating conundrum for Joe Mazzulla after Nuggets loss
item.description: Jayson Tatum started this week giving Chris Cenac Jr. a shoutout for his play during garbage time against the Mavericks. Five days later, Cenac Jr. was playing alongside the Celtics’ star while guarding the Nuggets’ top scorer (Jamal Murray) in crunch time. The rapid rise of the 19-year-old has been unexpected this week but sticks out as a bright spot for Boston amid back-to-back losses to the Magic and Nuggets. Cenac Jr. finished with six points and six rebounds in 17 minutes off the bench in Boston’s 105-101 loss to the Nuggets but his front line combination with Neemias Queta provided several promising moments on the glass and with his hustle plays. The strong play earned him some praise yet again from Joe Mazzulla as he outperformed free agent addition Mitchell Robinson off the bench. “I thought he was good,” Mazzulla told reporters in Denver. “He has a level of talent and athleticism and has the ability to make plays on both ends of the floor. He’s really versatile. He can guard point guards. He did a decent job in the first half on Aaron Gordon and matching that type of physicality. Taking some pressure off PG and JT having to defend them. “He has the versatility, he’s got the toughness, he’s got the athleticism, he’s got the talent. He just needs the reps to get better and better. I thought that was a bright spot from tonight was just kind of his growth from Game 1 to Game 2, he’s just gotta keep it up.” With the Celtics struggling on the defensive glass to begin the year (21st in the NBA), the prospect of handing more playing time to Cenac Jr. now is an intriguing proposition given the rookie’s untapped potential. The first-round pick provides the ability to switch with size defensively and take some wear and tear off of Boston’s star wings should be a priority over a regular-season grind. With Robinson struggling on most nights right now, Cenac Jr. has been the big off the bench this week that can help the most on that front. Mazzulla could try to invest more into Cenac Jr. now to experiment with what the rookie can bring to the table with regular minutes but that won’t necessarily be a smooth road given his inexperience. However, the prospect of regular minutes for Cenac Jr. or even allowing him some chances to start alongside Queta in certain matchups would help some of Boston’s weaknesses this year and potentially provide a spark. Ultimately, like Hugo González last season, the Celtics look like they found another steal at the end of the first round. How hard they want to push on the athletic 6-foot-11 amid his rapid rise will be a fascinating choice for Mazzulla as he balances wins and the potential Cenac Jr. could bring. item.title: After 66 at CME, Charley Hull dishes on the detox needed to win in 2016
item.description: NAPLES, FL — Charley Hull won the CME Group Tour Championship 10 years ago. Much has changed since then, including the winner's check, which has ballooned from $500,000 to $4 million. After an opening 66 on Thursday, a now 30-year-old Hull marveled at how quickly the decade had passed and how chubby she looked in those photos, blaming it on the discovery of American peanut butter and jelly sandwiches. Asked how her game has changed over the past 10 years, Hull said she didn't take golf seriously back then. "I remember coming into this event 10 years ago when I won like, hungover," she said. "I was out Thursday, Friday, Saturday drinking with my friends and stuff. "My mum and dad was fuming when I come back Saturday. Dad was like, 'So bad with what you done as preparation. You're meant to be a professional athlete. You're going to miss the cut this week. I turned round to him and I was like, 'Dad, there is no cut, so ha.' " Once Hull arrived at the Ritz Carlton in Naples, Florida, she messaged her friends back home and said she needed a massive detox. She holed up with Netflix and wounded up winning her first of three career titles. Now, back at the same Ritz with her family, including her father, Dave, who traveled to the U.S. for the first time since 2017, Hull hopes to wrap up a season of close calls with the biggest payday of her career. Then, after her WTGL debut on Tuesday, she plans to go off-grid. She'll buy a Nokia phone and completely switch off from the world. "If anyone wants to get hold of me, call me on that phone," she said, "like I'm done with texting; I'm done with social media. I just want to have a whole month detox." item.title: Travis Kelce’s actions at Kansas City Chiefs training camp proved his ‘impossible’ trait, says Brett Veach
item.description: Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Kansas City chiefs general manager Brett Veach says he continues to be amazed by Travis Kelce’s resilience. Travis Kelce is in his 14th NFL season, and he is not taking any shortcuts. The tight end has played in every game this season for the Kansas City Chiefs, despite just turning 37. Speaking to the Move The Sticks podcast, Brett Veach commented, “It is almost impossible to keep him off the field.” Kelce suffered an injury against the Falcons, aggravating an ankle injury where he reported soreness earlier in the season. He had returned to the game by halftime. Speaking about his conversation with Chiefs head athletic trainer Rick Burkholder, Veach explained: “One series into the Falcons game, he gets twisted up on the same ankle. With No. 4 UCLA coming to Ann Arbor on Saturday, the team is now dealing with a legal issue involving one of its top playmakers. Sophomore wide receiver Andrew Marsh has been charged with misdemeanor indecent exposure stemming from an off-campus incident in February. According to police, the alleged incident involved a female delivery driver who was dropping off food at a home. Marsh’s Rocky Sophomore Season Marsh emerged as one of Michigan’s breakout stars as a freshman in 2025, leading the team in receptions, receiving yards, and receiving touchdowns. The former four-star recruit from Katy, Texas, finished that season with 45 catches for 651 yards and four touchdowns. He still leads the Wolverines with 48 receptions this season, to go along with 459 receiving yards and one touchdown. But ball security has been a problem, as he has fumbled three times, including two on punt returns that cost him his spot on special teams. The charge also comes during a disappointing season for Michigan. The Wolverines are 5-5 overall and 2-5 in Big Ten play, and Whittingham fired offensive coordinator Jason Beck earlier this month after a loss to Michigan State. Michigan closes its home schedule against undefeated UCLA on Saturday before closing the regular season against rival Ohio State. Indecent Exposure Charge Marsh is facing a single misdemeanor charge of indecent exposure in the 14A-1 District Court, according to court records, via MLive . The charge stems from an incident at a home in the 5000 block of E. Spaniel Drive in Pittsfield Township. According to a release from the Pittsfield Township Police Department, which did not directly identify Marsh, the suspect exposed himself to a female delivery driver when she was dropping off food. “The complainant left the residence and subsequently received a message from the customer stating that she was attractive and asking if she would return to the address,” the department said in the release. The charge was authorized in October, and Marsh, now 19, is set to be arraigned on Dec. 2 before District Court Judge J. Cedric Simpson. Indecent exposure is typically punishable in Michigan by up to one year in jail, a $1,000 fine, or both. The Inter Miami captain is still comfortably the league’s top earner, on a guaranteed compensation of $28.3m. Robert Lewandowski (Chicago Fire) and Antoine Griezmann (Orlando City) have entered the list with the second and third highest wages, while Atlanta United’s Breel Embolo, another summer signing, ranks fifth on a guaranteed compensation of $10.8m. item.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
item.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it. But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio . From one of the absolute greats. Continue reading...

item.title: Inside women’s football’s difficult rise in Syria: ‘A joy that everyone in the country needed’
item.description: A 14-year civil war ravaged the country and ground women’s football to a halt. Today, the first glimmers of hope are beginning to emerge amid difficulty In December 2024, Syria’s under-18 women’s football team boarded a last-minute bus at midnight from Aqaba, bound for Damascus. The players had been in Jordan preparing for their final match of the WAFF women’s championship, where a win against Saudi Arabia would have kept their hopes of winning the title alive. Syria pulled out amid fears that the border would close. Back home, a war that had been largely frozen for four years was suddenly moving at pace. item.title: Spain in pain as historic run ends but De la Fuente feels best is yet to come
item.description: While the head coach, players and Spanish press were magnanimous in defeat, there was pride mixed in with disappointment – and confidence the future is still bright “With every game, defeat gets closer,” Luis de la Fuente had said and on Sunday night it finally came. Spain had lost only one competitive game since Scotland in March 2023 back when the coach hadn’t won anything and didn’t look like he ever would – and that solitary loss was on penalties in the 2025 Nations League final . Statistically, they said, penalties don’t count, so while Portugal lifted the trophy that night, the team that won the European Championship and World Cup in the summers either side also claimed a Fifa record of 44 official games unbeaten. And then England turned up at the Metropolitano . A night that started with Iker Casillas, Fernando Torres and Fernando Llorente handing the World Cup to Unai Simón ended with Spain trying to overhaul a shock 3-0 deficit. Against 10 men and led by a superb Lamine Yamal, Spain made De la Fuente think for a while that they would too, but it wasn’t to be. Continue reading...

item.title: Do good club managers necessarily make good international managers? | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: In a mailbag edition of our newsletter, we look at Mauricio Pochettino, Pep Guardiola’s international credentials and the lack of elite English managers Sign up for our free newsletter here Who should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager? – Tom S Although the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. That’s the positive from appointing from within; appointing from without is almost certainly more expensive and there’s the danger the next foreign manager does just what Mauricio Pochettino does, and has his head turned by the first vaguely attractive European job that comes calling. item.title: Familiarity of Doha drives home just how far Socceroos have come in recent years | Joey Lynch
item.description: There is increasing evidence of an evolution not only in approach but also mentality, highlighted by a return to the scene of Asian Cup heartbreak Last week’s 3-0 dismissal of Qatar at the Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium marked the first time the Socceroos had returned to the Gulf state since their heartbreaking elimination from the Asian Cup just under three years ago. Back then, coach Graham Arnold called Doha a “home away from home” after they relocated there during the Covid pandemic, and went so far as to suggest that they would have some form of advantage at the 2022 World Cup as a result. Wandering around the city in 2026, memories rush back of Socceroos fans becoming eager participants in the takeover of the city’s souks during the World Cup. So too the feelings of sadness to see the birds still cooped up in small cages at the nearby bird market. It evokes recollections of trips on the red Metro line out to the Al Janoub Stadium in Al Wakrah, aided by the faded posters and stickers celebrating the 2022 tournament’s arrival that to this day can still be seen in shopfronts. There’s the excitement, for some, when a stray cat reminds you just how personable the local felines can be, as well as the sense of unease that remains whenever one pauses to reflect on how all this was built and the hands that did so. item.title: WSL talking points: Chelsea’s gamble pays off and have Arsenal lost fear factor?
item.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. Ivanovic, you see, was not named Serbia captain until 2012 and Mikel, who was but a whippersnapper at 22 when the 2009-10 season started, was still seven years from getting his hands on the Nigeria armband. item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
